_about: Which category gets which of the eight category hues (--cat-1 ... --cat-8 in shared/design/lumebook.css; 0 = neutral ink). Builds read this file through shared/design/design.py: design.head() inlines a class per item (.lb-<class>-<key>, e.g. .lb-ws-creators), categories() and cat_class() give the data, category_css() writes aliases for a page's own class names. Pages without a build (dashboard, SMM plan) link categories.css, which `tools/lumebook.py sync` writes from this file and copies next to their lumebook.css. A set is one page's (or one concept's) 3 to 8 stable categories that a reader scans or filters by; keep a category on the same number everywhere it appears and give the categories of one set different numbers. Never colour status (done, late, broken) or the carousel pillars (kid, expert) with these hues. Where a page also shows status chips, prefer 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7: 1 sits near warning, 3 near success and 8 near the gold accent.
